subtitle: The town the Wasting paused
canonNote: Hallow's Creek, the first settlement the Wasting took, paused mid-second fifty years before the books, too perfect: white houses, white picket fences without a speck of peeling paint, roses of red quartz, pristine gravel, no wind, no birds (b1 ch.17:269; ch.21:11-19), and only its people grey stone; the white fences, the baker in his doorway, the ball in the air, the townsfolk stone to the skin with living eyes, the broken bridge's slabs hanging over the chasm, the crater with the red door at its heart, the Old Archive and the hungry shadows (CANON, book1 ch.15-21; world_bible). CANON-EXPANDED: the Bureau holding the town and cutting memory-quartz from the paused (book1 ch.3: geodes are fossilised memory), the Hollow as what the cut leaves, the bell tower with a painted dial a minute short of noon (no works). GAME-ONLY: every person, camp, the wings, the Waking Hour as a worked thing, the wagon. Kept out: the Archive's vault, the red door's riddle, the Prism, Hollow children. The people of chapters 19 and 21 (Mr Gable and Martha, Mrs Miller, the children, Talla by the willow) and the Square as chapter 21 tells it: Docs/REWORK_LOWTOWNS_HALLOWS.md picks 1, 2, 3 and 12. Docs/DUNGEON2_DESIGN.md. A valley town seen from the lip (CANON-EXPANDED, b1 ch.19:31; ch.17:267): the gatehouse on the lip, Main Street falling eight metres to the Square on the valley floor; two roads in, the high road over the slabs and the low road from the Fallen Mason's slab along the chasm's wall and through the Cellars (GAME-ONLY): REWORK_LOWTOWNS_HALLOWS.md picks 4 and 5.
roadsNote: the Ash Road, Main Street and the wagon track
squallText: A time-squall blows in over the town: the ash in it glitters silver, and for a breath your shadow is a step behind you.
worldMapNote: East of Oakhaven, past the Road's End, in the grey.

ride.name: The black-iron wagon
ride.shut: The wagon is the Picker-Master's: his teamsters will not let a stranger up while he stands.
ride.text: The mules lean into the traces. The wagon creaks out of the yard, round the chasm's east head on the Bureau's track and down to the milestone, where the grey thins. Nobody looks back at the town; it does not look back either.

secrets.name: Bet's Packed Cart
secrets.text: The cart is packed for the road west, and nothing on it has moved in fifty years: a chair lashed on top, a quilt, and under the seat a tin box, and in it a ring on a cord.

secrets.name: The Reed Chest

secrets.name: The Ringers' Chalked Names
secrets.prompt: Read the names chalked on the tower wall
secrets.text: Chalked low on the tower's inside wall in four hands: the ringers' names and a day of the week, the way bell-ringers mark a practice. The last one stops half way through the word.

props.name: Mr Gable
props.text: Mr Gable, the baker, in his doorway with a tray of loaves, stone to his apron strings. His eyes are blue. Human. Wet. They shift, just a fraction, following you. Behind him on the counter is a pie: stone crust, stone smoke standing over it in a perfect spiral. You smell blueberries. The bell over his door has not rung for fifty years; it would take only a step inside.
props.canonStatus: CANON (b1 ch.21:23, 32-36, 64-70: the baker in his doorway, his eyes, the pie; ch.21:VI, 368: his name)

props.name: Mrs Miller
props.interact: Look at the woman at the line
props.text: Mrs Miller, hanging out her washing, stone from her headscarf to her shoes, a sheet half up and a peg in her fingers. The line is as rigid as steel wire. Nothing on it has stirred in fifty years: there is no wind here. Her eyes, blue and wet, are not on the sheet. They are on you.
props.canonStatus: CANON (b1 ch.21:23: the woman at a laundry line as rigid as steel wire; ch.21:376: Mrs. Miller hanging laundry)

props.name: A child chasing the ball
props.text: Two children chase a ball that hangs in the air over the gravel, their laughter silenced for fifty years. The nearer one's mouth is open on it still. A dog has leapt after the ball with them and stopped a metre off the ground.
props.canonStatus: CANON (b1 ch.21:23: two children and the ball suspended in the air; ch.21:122: frozen children mid-laugh and dogs suspended in mid-air)

props.name: Talla
props.text: A girl of eleven or twelve, stone to the skin, thrown down over a hollow in the ash by the willow as if to shield someone small from the sky. There is no one under her now. The hollow is dug out, the ash heaped back on either side by a big pair of hands, years ago. Her eyes are open, blue and wet, and they are on the empty hollow. Someone has cut her name into the willow's stone bark beside her, in careful letters: TALLA.
props.canonStatus: CANON (Chris, 2026-10-18: the stone girl by the willow is Talla, Valen's sister; b1 ch.19:39, 53: his older sister threw herself over him by the weeping willow and was petrified; Gorm dug him out ten years before the book; b1 ch.17:300: her name); the name cut in the bark GAME-ONLY; the books' contradiction (ch.17:300-374, Talla dies of the Grey Rot) settled by Chris for the game

props.name: The chapel's glass
props.text: The chapel's windows are empty. Their stained glass burst outward with the sound the sky made when it tore, and it is still bursting: red, blue, gold and green shards hanging in the air before every window, a hand's breadth out and two metres out, stopped where they flew.
props.canonStatus: CANON (b1 ch.19:53); the glass stopped in the air CANON-EXPANDED (the town paused, b1 ch.21)

props.name: The crater's rim
props.text: The town hall is gone. In its place is a perfect hemisphere of missing reality: smooth glassy obsidian, curving fifty feet down into the dark to a floor that is a mirror. The whole town hangs upside down in it, roofs and chimneys and the tower, and none of it moves. Out over the middle a red door stands upright on a slab of floating marble, bright, wet, impossible red, its brass knocker a face with its lips sewn shut. Round it, slowly, go chairs and desks and bricks, a stone horse, the corner of a bank vault with its rebar sticking out like broken bones, a bench, a lamppost. The wind coming up out of it smells of ozone and old paper.

props.name: The chalked equations
props.interact: Read the chalk on the paving
props.text: Chalk on the paving, fifty years old and not a line of it smudged: rings within rings, spokes running in toward the crater's edge, small glyphs, and rows of working in a fast, sure hand. The middle of it went with the town hall. A High Scholar chalked it here to map the leylines under the valley; a girl touched the glyph at its centre.
props.canonStatus: CANON (b1 ch.19:49: Aethelgard's equations chalked onto the town square paving stones; Elara touched the central glyph); kept by the pause CANON-EXPANDED

props.name: The ancient town well
props.text: The ancient town well, older than any house on the Square, its stones worn smooth by a thousand buckets. A man stood here arguing with the town's elders on the morning the sky broke. The water down in it is still, and it does not reflect you.
props.canonStatus: CANON (b1 ch.19:41: Aethelgard near the ancient town well); the still water GAME-ONLY

props.name: The town below
props.text: Past the gate the valley opens below you. "Through the clearing fog, a town appeared." Picket fences. White houses. Main Street winds down in gentle slopes to the Square on the valley floor, and out of the Square the bell tower stands up, its painted dial a minute short of noon. Nothing down there moves.

The Hollow use it. The dust on its steps has no boot prints in it, only long smooth drag marks.

wings.name: The Granary on the race
wings.easeText: Word runs up Main Street ahead of you: the Granary has fallen. One of the Pact's watch at the tower door goes down the Granary road to see, and does not come back.

wings.name: The Cellars
wings.easeText: Under your feet the Cellars go quiet. In the Bell Tower one of Kersey's line is sent down to the well-house to find out why, and the tower's stair is the thinner for it.

checkpoints.name: The still lamp at the lip
The still lamp on Main Street
The still lamp by the Archive

waves.text: The bakery's bell gives one note. For a breath the room is warm and smells of bread; then the trapdoor lifts and the Hollow come up out of the cellar.
The bell rings again, a minute that will not end. More of them come up the cellar stair.
Boots on the Granary road: the Pact's relief comes up from the yard to take the Warden back.

waves.camp: Hollow up out of the well
waves.text: Something climbs out of the well-house: the Hollow, come up from the Cellars after the Warden.
Colour runs back into the town like water into a print. Below, the square moves; on the stair, two of the paused ringers wake and climb.
Two more of the ringers come up the stair, their faces still stone, their hands already on the rope that is not there.

glitches.name: The stone handcart
glitches.prompt: Lay a hand on the handcart's wheel
glitches.text: Under your hand the stone wheel turns. Colour runs up the lane: a man in a carter's apron leans into the shafts, laughing at something over his shoulder, and the handcart rolls on out of the lane between the Reed house and its neighbour, the way it was going fifty years ago.
glitches.endText: the lane beside the Reed house stays clear, a short way through to the creek and the Granary's footbridge.
glitches.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED (the Glitch: the bakery's bell and a minute of sun, book1 ch.21:82-112; the loop, ch.21:351); this moment GAME-ONLY

glitches.name: The hung slates
glitches.prompt: Touch the nearest of the hung slates
glitches.text: The slate you touch is warm. Sun pours through the broken roof, a slater's voice swears somewhere above, and the slates that have hung in the air for fifty years finish their fall: they land edge over edge on the old shelving and make a ramp of themselves up to the north gallery.
glitches.endText: the slates' ramp stands, a second way up onto the north gallery.
glitches.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED (the Glitch: the bakery's bell and a minute of sun, book1 ch.21:82-112; the loop, ch.21:351); this moment GAME-ONLY

glitches.name: The ford's splash
glitches.prompt: Put your hand into the stopped splash
glitches.text: The splash runs on. For a minute the creek is loud and brown and moving, and then it drops, a metre and more, as if something upstream had taken a breath; along the west bank the water drains out of the dark cellar's crawl and its door stands clear of the mud, open.
glitches.endText: the dark cellar's door stands open on the drained crawl, a way into the Cellars from the town.
glitches.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED (the Glitch: the bakery's bell and a minute of sun, book1 ch.21:82-112; the loop, ch.21:351); this moment GAME-ONLY

glitches.name: The well-boy
glitches.text: The boy finishes his run. He is nine, perhaps, freckled, a brass key on a string round his wrist, and he skids into the well-house shouting for his mother, drops the key into the trapdoor's lock and turns it, the way he was sent to. The bar beneath lifts with a knock.
glitches.endText: the well-house trapdoor stands unbarred, a way down into the Cellars from above.
glitches.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED (the Glitch: the bakery's bell and a minute of sun, book1 ch.21:82-112; the loop, ch.21:351); this moment GAME-ONLY
